evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Test methodology implementation and analytical outputs, including reconciliation, edge-case testing, data quality checks, and comparison against expected business or statistical results.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities emphasize meticulous validation, testing, reconciliation, and data quality throughout with no velocity/speed language present.
evidence.domain_risk: Work with business, actuarial, analytical, and technical stakeholders to understand the intended analytics methodology, data inputs, business rules, and expected outputs.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Insurance/actuarial context implies financial consequence but the JD's own language is generic methodology/data-engineering framing without explicit compliance, audit, or regulatory wording, so moderate per the tie-breaker.
evidence.data_team_maturity: Support the design, development, maintenance, and optimization of modern data pipelines and transformation logic using Databricks, SQL, Python, and lakehouse patterns.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Named tools (Databricks, SQL, Python) appear throughout responsibilities alongside existing pipelines to maintain and optimize, indicating a developing but not yet fully mature or early-stage function.
evidence.jd_authorship: Design derived tables, views, and curated data layers that align with analytical methodology and are suitable for consumption by front-end applications, dashboards, reports, and downstream users.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Precise, technically detailed responsibilities with named tools and specific methodology context make clear what this person does day to day.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: This person will work closely with actuarial analysts, developers, data engineers, and business stakeholders to understand analytical needs
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The primary audience is the internal data/analytics function and its methodology consumers (actuarial, engineering) rather than a specific commercial, product, or finance business unit.
evidence.autonomy_level: Build and/or apply analytics methodology on top of structured and semi-structured datasets using SQL, Python, and Databricks-based workflows.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Verbs are execution-oriented (build, apply, support, assist, test) receiving methodology and requirements from stakeholders rather than setting direction independently.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No mention of AI tools, AI coding assistance, or AI-consuming data infrastructure anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing: Test methodology implementation and analytical outputs, including reconciliation, edge-case testing, data quality checks, and comparison against expected business or statistical results.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and validation appear as an explicit owned responsibility with action verbs (test, validate) rather than only in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: ensure that methodology outputs are accurate, explainable, and production-ready
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate: emphasis is on accuracy, reliability, and production-readiness of analytical outputs rather than explicit compliance or regulatory risk language.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Support the design, development, maintenance, and optimization of modern data pipelines and transformation logic using Databricks, SQL, Python, and lakehouse patterns.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Responsibilities mix building new derived tables/methodology with maintaining, troubleshooting, and improving existing pipelines, with no dominant signal either way.
